Tests updated + e2e verified.

title: Per-page og:image gallery on the crawl detail page
description:
Collect the per-page og:image for every page in a crawl (not just the main page) and show a small gallery of those distinct images on the crawl detail page.

Motivation: a crawl covers many pages, each of which may declare its own OpenGraph image (`<meta property="og:image">`). Those are curated, page-level representative images — unlike arbitrary captured resources (icons/pixels/sprites), so no size/noise filtering is needed. A gallery of them gives a rich, honest visual overview of what a crawl contains, and photographs well.

Builds directly on rustyweb-crawl-thumbnail-s1ff, which already:
- extracts og:image per HTML record (search::extract_html_text -> HtmlText.og_image) — currently only the MAIN page's is used;
- has the fetch -> decode -> downscale -> cache pipeline (thumbnail.rs) and the /thumb serving route + CSS.

Scope for a future v1 (keep bounded):
- During indexing, collect og:image across pages, resolve each against its page URL, and DEDUP by resolved image URL (many pages share one site-wide default og:image, so distinct images are what matter).
- Cap the set per crawl (e.g. <= 12-24 distinct images) to bound index time + disk.
- Cache each as a downscaled thumbnail (e.g. <home>/index/thumbs/<crawl_id>/<n>.jpg) and record the set on the manifest, or a manifest sidecar.
- Serve them (extend the /thumb route to an indexed set, or a per-crawl gallery listing) and render a strip/grid on the crawl detail page. The single representative image (main page og:image) stays as the card/hero.
- Graceful: crawls with no per-page og:images just show the single representative image (or placeholder).

Considerations:
- Dedup + cap ordering: prefer distinct images; order by page order / seed pages first.
- Storage growth: N thumbnails per crawl * many crawls — keep N small; needs a reindex to populate.
- This is the "keep it simple, page-level OpenGraph metadata" version the maintainer wanted — explicitly NOT a dump of all captured image resources (that raw-gallery idea was considered and rejected as noisy/expensive).

Relates to s1ff (done) and rustyweb-collection-group-by-site-mwg1. Priority: future / P3.

title: Representative image/thumbnail for collection cards, collection detail, and crawl detail (from WACZ screenshots)
description:
Idea (maintainer): use a representative image to make collection cards and detail pages (and crawl detail pages) more visual -- rather than the current text-only cards/lists. This matters for the shareable/adoption story and for the blog post's screenshots.

Source of the image: Browsertrix WACZs often contain page screenshots, stored as WARC resource records (target URIs like `urn:view:<url>`, `urn:thumbnail:<url>`, `urn:screenshot:<url>`, image/png|jpeg payloads). We already consume a sibling record type -- Browsertrix's rendered-text `urn:text:` records (index.rs:674+, RenderedText) -- so this extends that same pattern to image records. Verify the exact URN scheme / content types against a real Browsertrix WACZ before committing to field names.

Scope (v1, keep it small):
- Pick ONE representative image per crawl (WACZ): e.g. the thumbnail/screenshot of the seed page (first page in pages.jsonl), preferring `urn:thumbnail:` if present (small) else downsizing a larger screenshot. Don't ingest all screenshots.
- Store just enough to serve it: record the chosen image's location (which inner WARC + offset/length, consistent with CDX-guided extraction) on the crawl's manifest entry, OR extract+cache the bytes under <home>/index (decide; caching avoids a range fetch on every card render but costs disk). Lean toward a small cached thumbnail (e.g. index/thumbs/{wacz_id}.jpg) so serving is cheap and works for local + remote sources uniformly.
- Serve it: a route like /thumb/{wacz_id} (or /crawl/{id}/thumb) returning the cached image with caching headers, mirroring serve_embedded_asset's ETag/Cache-Control.
- Display it: collection card (homepage), collection detail (a representative image, likely from one member crawl), and crawl detail. Collection-level image = pick one member's thumbnail (e.g. first/most-recent member) for v1.
- Graceful fallback: many WACZs (esp. non-Browsertrix, e.g. py-wacz) have NO screenshots -- must degrade cleanly to today's text-only card/detail. No broken image boxes.

Considerations:
- Only extract during indexing (index_one), alongside the existing record pass, to avoid a second scan. Optional flag to disable (privacy/size).
- Size/perf: thumbnails should be small (cap dimensions/bytes); consider re-encoding to JPEG/WebP. Adds an image dep (e.g. `image` crate) -- weigh against the single-binary/pure-Rust ethos (image is pure Rust; OK).
- Privacy/appropriateness: a screenshot may show sensitive content; keep it opt-outable and only use the seed/representative page.

Relates to the vocab rename (crawls-captures-vocab-b1e) and faceted detail pages (facets-detail-pages-dgr) -- together these are the collection/crawl view polish pass. Ties to the Browsertrix importer epic (15z), which brings in exactly these screenshot-bearing WACZs.
close_reason: Delivered, with an og:image pivot: SUCHO/2022 crawls have no Browsertrix screenshots (zero urn: records), so the representative image is the crawl's main-page og:image (twitter:image fallback) instead. Pipeline: at index time (CDX-streamable WACZs), thumbnail::generate reads the main page's HTML, extracts og:image, range-fetches that captured image from the WACZ, downscales it (image crate, 400px), and caches <home>/index/thumbs/<crawl_id>.jpg. Served at GET /thumb/{id}; shown on collection cards + collection/crawl detail. No image => CSS-only placeholder (hash-tinted gradient, per the maintainer's suggestion). Best-effort throughout; needs a reindex to populate. Screenshot-source + per-collection curated images remain follow-ups.

title: Vocabulary: Crawls / Captures vs WACZ in the UI
description:
Question (maintainer): do users care more about "Crawls" or "Captures" than about a "WACZ"?

WACZ is a packaging format -- a technical container. Users of a web archive more likely think in terms of:
- Crawls: a crawl session (e.g. a Browsertrix crawl) -- the user-meaningful activity that produced the content. Often 1:1 with a WACZ today, but not necessarily (a WACZ could bundle multiple crawls; a crawl could span WACZs).
- Captures / mementos: individual snapshots of a URL at a point in time -- what users navigate temporally (repeat captures of the same URL over time; already grouped in results, per the Costa & Silva navigational/temporal finding cited in DESIGN).

This is an information-architecture / vocabulary decision, not (yet) code: audit where the UI foregrounds "WACZ" and decide whether "Crawl" and/or "Capture" would be clearer -- e.g. presenting a WACZ as a "crawl" in provenance/collection contexts while keeping "WACZ" only where the file/format is actually meant (downloads, fixity, replay source). Ties to the two-level collection model and the provenance framing (Maemura et al.).

Worth deciding the mental model rustyweb presents before layering more UI (facets on detail pages, cross-WACZ discovery) on top of it, since those features inherit whatever vocabulary we choose. Discussion/decision issue; the outcome may spawn concrete rename/relabel tasks.
close_reason: Relabeled the UI to lead with 'Crawl': /wacz/{id} -> /crawl/{id} (route + handler + view), collection 'Crawls' count/heading, 'N crawls' on cards, crawl-detail empty states. Kept WACZ for file/format contexts (index/reindex CLI, /files byte-range, replay source, fixity) and the data model (Wacz/waczs.json). Documented the vocab split in DESIGN. 'Captures'/mementos vocab remains a separate later concern (out of scope).

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Decision (maintainer, after using the app): lead with "Crawl" as the primary user-facing noun. Most users don't care about WACZ (a packaging format); they think in terms of crawls. So this moves from an open IA question to a concrete relabel/rename task.

Direction:
- Present a WACZ as a "Crawl" in user-facing surfaces: the /wacz/{id} detail page becomes the crawl view; collection pages list "Crawls" (not "WACZs"); homepage cards say "N crawls" (not "N WACZs").
- Keep "WACZ" ONLY where the file/format is genuinely meant: the crawl detail "File" section (Source / Size / SHA-256 / download), the replay source, fixity/integrity, and the `rustyweb index archive/*.wacz` CLI docs.
- Route: consider renaming /wacz/{id} -> /crawl/{id} (early, few users, cleaner long-term) with the old path optionally 301-redirecting; or keep /wacz/{id} internally and only change labels. Decide as part of the work.

Nuance to keep in mind (don't over-engineer now): in Browsertrix an item can be a "Crawl" OR an "Upload"; a crawl could in principle span multiple WACZs and a WACZ could bundle multiple crawls. Today it's ~1:1, so "Crawl" is a safe default label. Later we can refine from Browsertrix item metadata (15z.6) to say "Crawl" vs "Upload" precisely.

"Captures" / mementos (individual URL snapshots over time) remain a SEPARATE, later concern -- those are the temporally-grouped snapshots in search results, not this rename. Out of scope here.

Concrete surfaces to change (audited in views.rs):
- home card: "(c.count) WACZ[s]" -> "crawl[s]" (views.rs:162)
- home empty state text mentions archive/*.wacz (keep -- that's the CLI/format) (views.rs:153)
- collection page: h2 "WACZs" -> "Crawls"; "No WACZs in this collection." -> "No crawls ..." (views.rs:440-442)
- crawl (WACZ) detail: page framing/headings; "No pages are listed in this WACZ." -> "... in this crawl." (views.rs:520); keep the "File" section as WACZ/format.
- MemberItem / WaczPage struct + fn names can stay as-is internally (WACZ is correct at the data layer); this is a presentation-layer relabel.

Bumping to P2 and starting now (ties to the blog post / screenshots the maintainer is preparing). Relates to facets-on-detail (dgr) and representative-image (new) -- the three together are the collection/crawl view polish pass.

title: Cross-WACZ link resolution during replay
description:
Problem: replay is WACZ-direct and scoped to ONE WACZ. The viewer loads a single source (viewer_source(col) -> /replay/viewer?source=<wacz>&url=&ts=), so wabac.js resolves links only within that WACZ. If a replayed page links to a URL that isn't in the loaded WACZ but IS archived in ANOTHER WACZ in the collection/archive, the link fails to replay -- even though rustyweb has that URL indexed elsewhere. This undercuts the "reading room" goal of navigating the archive as a whole.

What we already have to build on:
- Tantivy index maps url -> collection/WACZ (+ timestamp) for indexed PAGES (fast, exact-match lookup on the url field).
- search-url opens each WACZ's internal CDX and returns records matching a URL, so it can resolve ANY archived URL (not just pages) to the WACZ(s) that hold it -- at the cost of reading CDXs.

Candidate approaches (to evaluate):
1. Index-driven redirect (lightweight): add a resolve API (e.g. GET /api/resolve?url= -> [{wacz_id, ts}]) backed by the index for pages. When a replayed page navigates to a URL the current WACZ lacks, consult the API and re-launch the viewer against the WACZ that has it (a "this link lives in another crawl -- open it" jump). Low browser footprint; needs a way to detect the miss / intercept navigation inside ReplayWeb.page.
2. Multi-WACZ collection replay (native): load a ReplayWeb.page multi-WACZ collection (a JSON manifest listing the collection's member WACZ sources) instead of a single WACZ, so wabac.js merges their indexes and resolves any URL present in the collection natively. Cleanest UX; but the browser loads each member WACZ's index -- a scale concern for large/institutional collections. VERIFY ReplayWeb.page multi-WACZ support + how it scopes/loads indexes.
3. Hybrid / lazy: start with the page's own WACZ; on a miss, resolve via the index and dynamically add the target WACZ to the wabac collection, so only WACZs actually needed get loaded.

Open questions:
- How to detect a cross-WACZ miss / hook link navigation inside the ReplayWeb.page iframe (does it expose events / postMessage, or do we intercept clicks pre-replay?).
- Page-level resolution (the click-a-link case) vs full resource-level (sub-resources like images/CSS from another WACZ) -- the latter is deeper and likely out of scope for v1.
- Scale: avoid loading an entire large collection's indexes into the browser (ties to rustyweb-scale-footprint-qw5).
- Which URL/timestamp to pick when multiple WACZs/captures have the target (closest in time? most recent? same collection first?).

Scope note: v1 could target page-to-page links within a single curated collection, resolved via the index, as the highest-value slice. Relates to the two-level collection model, search-url, and the outbound-links link-graph task (rustyweb-outbound-links-ind).
close_reason: WON'T FIX (maintainer decision, 2026-07-26): resolution WITHIN a collection is acceptable, so the explicit 'archived in another crawl - open it?' affordance won't be built. Multi-WACZ collection replay (bukh Phase 1 + qw5.10) already resolves links across a collection's member WACZs via wabac's pagesQueryUrl (/collection/{id}/pages) - silently, scoped to the collection; that within-collection resolution is the accepted model. Sub-resource transclusion stays out (role-2 lookup is destination-gated to page navigations), preserving per-page temporal coherence. The blocks-dependency on federation-shwl.3 (/api/resolve) is moot for dk4; that endpoint remains its own federation task.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Design caution (temporal coherence): relevant prior work from Michael Nelson's team at ODU (the WS-DL group) on temporal violations in composite mementos -- a replayed page can stitch together embedded resources captured at different times, yielding a composite that never actually existed as presented. See Ainsworth, Nelson & Van de Sompel, "Only One Out of Five Archived Web Pages Existed as Presented" (ACM Hypertext 2015), and the broader WS-DL work on temporal coherence / prima facie violations (the Internet Archive Wayback Machine transcluding older captures of embedded resources into a page).

Why it matters here: cross-WACZ resolution deliberately pulls a URL from a DIFFERENT WACZ -- i.e. a different crawl at a (possibly very) different time. Doing so can INTRODUCE exactly these temporal violations, presenting a page that never existed. So the "which WACZ/timestamp to pick" open question above is not just a convenience choice -- it is a correctness concern:
- Prefer captures close to the root page's memento-datetime; bound and/or surface the temporal spread to the user rather than silently substituting a far-off capture.
- Page-to-page link navigation (following a link to another archived page) is lower risk than transcluding a sub-resource (image/CSS/JS) from another WACZ into the current page -- the latter is the classic temporal-violation case and should be treated with extra caution (or left out of v1).
- Consider making cross-WACZ substitution visible/optional (e.g. "this link is archived in another crawl from <date> -- open it?") rather than seamless, so the user knows they've crossed a temporal boundary.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Design reframing (maintainer): single-WACZ replay scope is a FEATURE, not a bug. Because replay is scoped to one WACZ, a rendered page only pulls resources captured in that same crawl -- which is precisely what preserves temporal coherence and avoids the ODU-documented temporal violations (a page stitched from resources of different times that never existed as presented). Pulling a JS file or image from another time period into the page would be the bug; NOT doing so is the virtue.

Consequences for this feature:
- Do NOT merge WACZs for replay or transclude sub-resources (JS/CSS/images) across WACZs -- that would recreate the temporal-violation problem. This deprioritizes the "native multi-WACZ merged replay" approach and rules out cross-WACZ sub-resource resolution.
- Reframe the cross-WACZ case around MISSING PAGES (link targets), not resources: when a link's target isn't in the current WACZ, use the index to surface where else in the archive it was captured -- list the other WACZs/crawls that hold it, WITH their capture dates and provenance -- as an explicit discovery affordance. Opening one starts a fresh, temporally-coherent single-WACZ replay in THAT crawl's context.
- Make the temporal/provenance boundary explicit: the goal is to let the user consciously choose to look at another capture, understanding the crawl context is changing -- not to silently substitute content into the current page.

Net: this is primarily a DISCOVERY feature (fits the reading-room ethos: "this link isn't in this crawl; here's where else in the archive to find it, and when it was captured"), layered on index lookups -- not a replay-fidelity change. Single-WACZ replay stays coherent and untouched.

Documentation: when this is implemented, note the connection to web-archives research in README.md and DESIGN.md -- both temporal coherence / temporal violations (ODU WS-DL; Ainsworth, Nelson & Van de Sompel, HT 2015) and the framing of single-WACZ scope as a coherence feature. DESIGN.md already grounds the discovery features in the literature (Costa & Silva; Maemura et al.; the SHINE / SolrWayback lineage), so this fits alongside them.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Plan (wabac `pagesQueryUrl` mechanism + how it reconciles with the single-WACZ / temporal-coherence stance above)

## New intel: wabac.js has a server-side page-list API (`pagesQueryUrl`)
Reverse-engineered from the vendored bundle (replaywebpage 2.4.6, crates/rustyweb-lib/static/replay/sw.js). A collection can carry `metadata.pagesQueryUrl` (also read from a multi-WACZ replay.json). When set, wabac STOPS loading pages from the WACZ (`if(!this.pagesQueryUrl){…load pages.jsonl…}`) and calls the server instead. It is used in TWO distinct roles:

1. Page list + search (`queryPages`): `GET <pagesQueryUrl>?search=<q>&page=<n>&pageSize=<25>` → `200 {"total":N,"items":[{"url","ts"|"date","title","filename"},…]}`. Powers the viewer's Pages sidebar and in-replay search. Purely informational — no resources are transcluded.

2. URL→WACZ resolution for on-demand replay (`getWACZFilesForPagesQuery`): `GET <pagesQueryUrl>?url=<exact>&pageSize=25` (falls back to `?search=<url>`) → `items[].filename` → the member WACZ(s) holding that URL; wabac then lazily loads ONLY those WACZ files and serves the resource from them. `item.filename` must match a WACZ `name` in the collection's replay.json resource list.

This is the Browsertrix pattern — their public replay.json carries `pagesQueryUrl` pointing at their `/pages` API (we saw it on usgov-archive).

## The catch (re: the temporal-coherence reframing above)
Role 2 is exactly the cross-WACZ sub-resource transclusion this ticket rules out: wabac resolves ANY requested URL (incl. images/CSS/JS) to whichever WACZ has it and loads it into the current page — recreating the ODU temporal-violation problem. So we must NOT flip replay to a native merged multiwacz-with-pagesQueryUrl collection. That would undo the single-WACZ virtue.

## Proposed design: adopt role 1, not role 2
Keep rendering single-WACZ (temporally coherent). Use rustyweb's index only for discovery, via one endpoint that happens to be wabac-`pagesQueryUrl`-shaped so it can also feed the viewer's page list/search:

- New endpoint `GET /replay/<coll>/pages?search=&url=&page=&pageSize=` answered from the Tantivy index (we already map url→crawl/WACZ+ts, and have title/ts/collection). Returns `{total, items:[{url, ts, title, filename}]}`, `filename` = the crawl's WACZ resource name.
- Wire it as the collection's `pagesQueryUrl` ONLY to power the collection-wide **page list + search sidebar** in the existing single-WACZ viewer (role 1). This is a straight win: search/browse the whole collection's pages from the index, without loading pages.jsonl.
- For the **missing-link case** (the reframed core of this ticket): when a link target isn't in the current WACZ, hit the SAME endpoint (`?url=`) to find which other crawl(s) hold it, and surface an explicit "archived in another crawl from <date> — open it?" affordance (with provenance). Opening one launches a fresh single-WACZ replay in THAT crawl (approach #1 in the description). No transclusion; the temporal boundary is visible and user-chosen.
- Prefer captures closest to the current memento-datetime; show the temporal spread (per the temporal-coherence comment).

Open verification items:
- Confirm whether setting `pagesQueryUrl` on the viewer's single-WACZ collection triggers wabac's role-2 resource resolution at all, or only the page-list/search. If it can't be cleanly separated, drive the page list + miss-detection ourselves (UI/postMessage) and keep the endpoint purely as our own resolve API (overlaps rustyweb-federation-shwl.3 `/api/resolve`).
- How to detect the link miss / hook navigation inside the ReplayWeb.page iframe (still the key UX unknown from the description).
- Pin behavior to the vendored wabac version + add a replay test.

## Relationship to rustyweb-scale-footprint-qw5
Bidirectional, and the reason to prefer the server-side pages endpoint over loading pages.jsonl client-side:
- This IS the replay-client instance of qw5's "laptop→institutional TBs" goal. A large collection (e.g. usgov-archive's 570k-page collections) can't load its full page list into the browser's IndexedDB; `pagesQueryUrl` paginates server-side so the replay-client footprint stays flat regardless of collection size — complementing qw5's focus on the server index footprint.
- The pages endpoint is a paginated, searchable query over the SAME Tantivy index qw5 is modeling, so its cost belongs in qw5.5 (query-time cost of faceting/grouping at scale) as a new consumer, and qw5.3 (cap stored body text) bounds how cheaply it can return titles/snippets.
- Its latency depends on the index being compacted — a fragmented index makes this query slow the same way it slowed search (see qw5.9 optimize/merge). So dk4-via-pagesQueryUrl is ENABLED BY qw5's index being scale-ready and is itself a qw5-aligned scale win on the client side.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Clarification (request flow — does replay phone home per URL?): No. Normal resource replay stays WACZ-direct and does NOT round-trip to the rustyweb API per URL:
- Rendering the current page: wabac loads that ONE WACZ's index into the browser and resolves the page's own resources (HTML/img/CSS/JS) locally, fetching bytes via range reads on /files/{id} (a dumb byte server, not a resolve API). Unchanged from today.
- The pages API (pagesQueryUrl-shaped endpoint) is hit only on occasional, user-driven events: (a) the page-list/search sidebar (paginated, per user action), and (b) a cross-WACZ link MISS (only when a link target isn't in the current WACZ). Never per sub-resource.

Explicitly NOT adopted (these WOULD talk back per URL): wabac's `remotewarcproxy` source (fetches H/<url>+A/<url> from the server for every resource), and native multiwacz + pagesQueryUrl "role 2" (resolves each requested URL, incl. sub-resources, to a WACZ via the API and lazy-loads it) — the latter also being the temporal-violation trap.

Caveat to verify: setting pagesQueryUrl on the collection to get the sidebar MIGHT also switch on wabac's per-URL role-2 resolution — couldn't confirm from the minified bundle whether they separate. If not, fallback is to NOT set pagesQueryUrl and instead drive the sidebar + miss-detection ourselves (viewer/postMessage), so the API is touched only on explicit user actions. Either way the guarantee holds: normal resource replay does not round-trip to the API per URL.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
Aligns with rustyweb-homepage-replay-bukh (2026-07-25): both need the SAME missing primitive — a collection-level (multi-WACZ) replay. bukh's core builds it (homepage 'replay a collection'); dk4 layers cross-WACZ discovery on top. bukh naturally precedes dk4. Linked as related.

== Consolidated sw.js trace (replaywebpage 2.4.6, class Gb = multi-WACZ loader). Supersedes the earlier 'couldn't confirm from the minified bundle whether roles separate' open item. ==

MULTI-WACZ COLLECTION FORMAT (loadWACZFiles): a JSON doc with resources:[{name,path,hash,crawlId}] (+ optional metadata.pagesQueryUrl / preloadResources / textIndex / total). Same family as Browsertrix replay.json. Each path = a WACZ location -> maps directly onto rustyweb /files/{id} (local) or presigned/remote URL (streamed); members can independently be local or remote.

ROLE 2 (per-URL server resolution) IS DESTINATION-GATED — the sub-resource temporal-violation fear was OVERSTATED. getWACZFilesToTry sets the URL-to-resolve (r=t.url) only when destination is 'document'/'iframe' (top-level page nav); sub-resources (image/style/script/font) never reach getWACZFilesForPagesQuery. So cross-WACZ sub-resource transclusion (the ODU temporal-violation trap) does NOT happen via pagesQueryUrl. Only page navigations resolve across WACZs.

BUT two things still couple the roles:
1. Role 2 is SILENT, not explicit: a page-nav to a URL not in the current WACZ auto-resolves (?url=<href>&pageSize=25, falls back to ?search=) and lazy-loads that WACZ — no 'open it? from <date>' prompt. That's the explicit temporal-boundary UX dk4 wants; you can't get the Pages sidebar (role 1) via pagesQueryUrl without also getting this silent page-jump.
2. The machinery is json/multiwacz-gated ('json'===rootSourceType; retryLoad early-returns otherwise). Using pagesQueryUrl at all requires switching the viewer from single-WACZ to a multi-WACZ json collection.

TWO-MODE SCALE TABLE (shared with bukh, ties to qw5):
- multi-WACZ, NO pagesQueryUrl: wabac loads every member WACZ index client-side; native cross-WACZ page+subresource resolution; OK small, infeasible large.
- multi-WACZ + pagesQueryUrl: wabac skips per-WACZ page lists, defers URL->WACZ to the server endpoint, lazily loads only needed members; flat browser footprint; the only viable large-collection path.

CONTRACT if we set pagesQueryUrl (wabac appends): ?url=<exact>, ?search=<q> (fallback + page-list search), ?page=<n>, ?pageSize=25; expects {total, items:[{url, ts|date, title, filename}]} where item.filename must match a member WACZ name. Path is NOT prescribed (comes from metadata.pagesQueryUrl) — could be /replay/{coll}/pages or a global /api/resolve (sibling to the existing /api/search).

DESIGN CHOICE: (A) go multi-WACZ + pagesQueryUrl = native sidebar + silent cross-WACZ page jumps, sub-resources safe, but off single-WACZ and no explicit affordance; (B) stay single-WACZ, don't set pagesQueryUrl, drive sidebar + miss-detection ourselves (postMessage) against our own /api/resolve = full control over the explicit 'open it?' temporal-boundary UX, more code. Sub-resource safety holds either way, so the real trade is native-but-silent vs custom-but-explicit — a UX/ethos call, not a temporal-safety one.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: Shared foundation now IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-25, via bukh Phase 1, working tree): collection-level multi-WACZ replay (GET /collection/{id}/replay.json + viewer multiwacz support). dk4's cross-WACZ discovery now layers on this — mostly additive. Reaffirming the stance revision from the sw.js trace: multi-WACZ replay is safe for sub-resources (role-2 lookup is destination-gated to document/iframe), so the earlier 'rules out native multi-WACZ' framing should be softened in the description to 'avoid pagesQueryUrl role-2 SILENT page-jumps if we want the explicit affordance'.

title: Batched collection delete (avoid a commit per member crawl)
description: index::delete_collection with_crawls calls delete_crawl per member, each opening a Tantivy writer, committing, and rewriting the manifest -> O(N) commits + manifest saves for an N-crawl collection. Add a batched path: one writer/commit and a single manifest save for the whole collection. Correctness-first version shipped in PR #79; this is the performance follow-up. Relates to rustyweb-atomic-reindex-7x3j.

title: Dedupe the delete 'danger zone' markup across crawl/collection views
description: views.rs writes the details.danger-zone + confirm-delete form separately in the crawl and collection views (they differ only by the with-crawls checkbox/text). Extract a small maud helper (action, prompt, optional checkbox) so a change is made once. Minor cleanup from the PR #79 review.

title: Reclaim index disk after delete (force a segment merge)
description:
FINDING (2026-08-21, from real use): running `optimize` after deleting many crawls did NOT reclaim index disk. Root cause: optimize only expunges deleted docs when it actually MERGES segments (a merge rewrites a segment without its tombstoned docs). It merges down toward --max-segments (default 8), so an index already at <= 8 segments merges nothing -> no reclamation. optimize's garbage_collect_files only removes orphaned files from completed merges; it does not expunge deletes on its own, and Tantivy has no expunge-deletes-without-merge. Workaround today: `optimize --max-segments 1` forces a full merge (transient ~2x disk). 

Fix options to consider: (1) crawl/collection delete triggers a reclaim; (2) add an optimize mode / flag that force-merges any segment carrying deletes regardless of segment count (expunge-deletes), not just when count > target; (3) after delete, if deleted-doc ratio is high, force a merge. Whichever, the trigger must not be gated on segment-count > target.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #90 (merged): optimize now runs an expunge-deletes pass that rewrites any segment carrying tombstones regardless of --max-segments, so a delete reclaims disk without the --max-segments 1 workaround.

title: Crawl delete: redirect can 404 for a legacy singleton collection
description: delete_crawl_handler redirects to /collection/{collection}. For a legacy WACZ whose collection is a migration-synthesized singleton (collection id == crawl id, no real Collection entry), deleting the sole crawl leaves that URL resolving to nothing -> 404. Fix: when the crawl was the last member (plan.last_in_collection) and the collection has no finding-aid entry, redirect home (or to the collection only when it still exists). Found in the PR #79 code review.

title: Deployment: prebuilt binaries (local) + Docker (server)
description: Two audiences, two paths. (1) LOCAL/try-it: prebuilt binaries + a quickstart so someone can download, run 'indice serve', and see indice in a browser without a build toolchain. (2) SERVER: a Docker image + docker-compose (indice + Caddy for automatic HTTPS) as the one-command self-host recipe. Single self-contained binary with embedded assets makes both tractable. Explicitly NOT the Tauri/desktop-app path for now. Carries the indice-specific requirements from the closed prod-deploy-mhx: byte-range passthrough for WACZ replay, no double-compression / never gzip a range response, run non-root on loopback (serve is read-only), CORS same-origin-vs-remote, a /health route. Relates to rustyweb-object-storage-home (cloud storage backing).

title: Release CI: build + publish prebuilt binaries to GitHub Releases
description: A GitHub Actions workflow that, on a version tag, cross-compiles the indice binary and attaches archives to a GitHub Release. Assets are embedded at build time so each binary is self-contained. OPEN: target set — macOS (arm64 + x86_64), Linux (x86_64 + arm64), Windows? (start mac+Linux). macOS 'download & run' is quarantined by Gatekeeper unless signed/notarized — v1 can document the xattr workaround; signing/notarization is a follow-up. Use --locked builds.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #96 (merged): release CI builds prebuilt binaries for mac/Linux/Windows on native runners with checksums (draft→publish), plus a bundled apod.wacz sample and a README quickstart. Validated on real macOS + Raspberry Pi 4.

title: YunoHost app package for indice
description:
Package indice as a YunoHost app so it installs in a couple of clicks on a personal YunoHost server (Debian-based; common on a Raspberry Pi). Sibling to the Homebrew (.8) / Scoop (.9) install channels — lower priority.

Shape: a YunoHost app package (manifest.toml v2 + scripts/{install,remove,upgrade,backup,restore} + conf/{systemd service, nginx snippet}). indice fits the model well: run 'indice serve' as a systemd service bound to a local port, non-root, index read-only; YunoHost's nginx reverse-proxies it with automatic Let's Encrypt TLS.

indice-specific notes to carry in:
- Reuse the prebuilt linux-gnu release archives from deploy-wo6l.1 — the install script downloads the archive matching the server arch (aarch64 for a Pi, x86_64 otherwise), rather than building from source. Multi-arch selection required.
- BYTE-RANGE passthrough: YunoHost's nginx must pass Range/Accept-Ranges/Content-Range to /files/{id} and not buffer multi-GB WACZs (proxy_buffering off / proxy_max_temp_file_size 0 for that location). Same requirement as the general proxy story.
- Management mode via YunoHost SSO: indice's forward-auth (--auth-proxy-header + --auth-proxy-secret, already built) can integrate with YunoHost's SSOwat — map the portal's authenticated-user header to indice and inject the shared secret in the nginx conf, so /manage is gated by the YunoHost login while the read-only site stays public. Decide public-read vs SSO-gated per the app config.
- Storage: <home> (archive/ + index/) under the app's data dir; backup/restore scripts must cover it (archive can be large — stream-only keeps it small; document both).
- A /health route (deploy-wo6l.3) helps the service/proxy readiness check.

Publishing: a ynh-app git repo passing YunoHost's package_check/linter, then submit to the app catalog (apps.yunohost.org). Depends on deploy-wo6l.1 (release artifacts); benefits from deploy-wo6l.3 (/health).

title: Build + publish multi-arch Docker image to GHCR on release
description:
Publish a versioned, multi-arch Docker image to GHCR on each release tag — the server-side analog of the prebuilt binaries (deploy-wo6l.1). Depends on the Dockerfile (deploy-wo6l.4).

Registry: ghcr.io/edsu/indice, authenticated with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN (permissions: packages: write) — first-party, no external account, consistent with the binaries' no-third-party-actions stance.

Multi-arch amd64 + arm64 (so it runs on x86 servers AND a Raspberry Pi). Build each arch on its NATIVE runner (ubuntu-24.04 + ubuntu-24.04-arm) and combine into one manifest (docker buildx imagetools create / docker manifest), rather than buildx+QEMU emulation (Rust compiles far too slowly under emulation). Use the Docker CLI directly (docker build/login/imagetools) to keep the release path free of third-party actions.

Tags: :vX.Y.Z plus :latest. Gate :latest (and possibly all pushes) to non-prerelease tags so the v*-test dry-run tags don't clobber :latest. Wire into the existing release workflow (a new job on the same tag trigger) or a sibling workflow.

Optional hardening (later): pin the base images (rust:<ver>-bookworm, distroless/cc-debian12) by digest for reproducibility. Relates to deploy-wo6l.5 (compose can then reference the published image instead of building).
close_reason: Merged via PR #102: native per-arch GHCR image build + digest-merge manifest on release.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: PR #102 (off main). Native per-arch build (amd64 on ubuntu-22.04, arm64 on ubuntu-22.04-arm, no QEMU) → push by digest → docker-manifest merges into :{version} always + :latest for final releases only. docker CLI + GitHub artifact actions only (no 3rd-party). actionlint clean. NOTE: first release creates the GHCR package PRIVATE — make it public once for anonymous docker pulls.

title: Deploy on a container cloud platform (Droplet/VM or managed PaaS: Fly.io, Render, DO App Platform)
description: Document (and/or automate) deploying indice on a container-based cloud host. Two shapes: (a) a plain VM/Droplet running the docker-compose + Caddy stack (SITE_ADDRESS=domain -> auto-HTTPS) — reuses deploy-wo6l.5 directly; persistent local disk, most flexible. (b) a managed container/PaaS pointing at the GHCR image (DigitalOcean App Platform, Fly.io, Render, Railway) — managed TLS/restarts, but their ephemeral filesystems need a persistent volume or an object-storage home for archive+index (ties to rustyweb-object-storage-home-7li7). Start with (a): a short 'deploy on a Droplet/VM' guide in the docs; then evaluate one managed PaaS (Fly.io is container-native and simple). Optional: a DO Marketplace 1-click image. User interested (raised again 2026-09).

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: 2026-10-03: overlaps epic rustyweb-demo-instance-5b9k, which deploys a real instance at app.indice.page on an UpCloud VM using the existing compose + Caddy stack - i.e. shape (a) from this ticket's description. 5b9k.9 adds a compose.demo.yaml overlay and a runbook guide; 5b9k.10 does the provisioning. The ephemeral-filesystem concern noted here is answered by 5b9k.1-.3 (WACZ bytes in a bucket). Close this into that epic once .9/.10 land, or keep it only for the managed-PaaS shape (b).

title: Full identity-provider (SSO) support for management via oauth2-proxy
description: Upgrade path beyond the Caddy basic_auth stopgap (deploy-wo6l.5). Document (and optionally ship as a compose overlay) putting oauth2-proxy in front of indice's management surface so admins log in with Google/GitHub/OIDC. indice's forward-auth is unchanged: oauth2-proxy performs the login and sets X-Forwarded-User (and Caddy still injects X-Indice-Auth-Secret), so this is a drop-in replacement for the basic_auth block in Caddyfile.manage. Needs operator-supplied OAuth client id/secret + allowed users/domain, so it can't be fully turnkey — provide a documented example + env template. Supersedes the basic_auth stopgap for real multi-admin/SSO deployments.
close_reason: Done: oauth2-proxy SSO shipped (PR #105); compose.sso.yaml + Caddyfile.sso present in tree.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: SSO + .14 interaction: the .14 indice changes (can_login, /manage/login bounce, identity-from-header) are proxy-agnostic — no rework needed for SSO. /manage/login works as a universal login entry (basic_auth prompt OR oauth2-proxy OIDC redirect). ONLY the Caddyfile public-route block differs: basic_auth uses a one-line '@maybe_auth header Authorization *'; oauth2-proxy needs an OPTIONAL auth subrequest to /oauth2/auth via forward_auth + handle_response that proceeds anonymously on 401 (not the redirecting default) and copies X-Auth-Request-Email>X-Forwarded-User on 2xx. Secret can be injected unconditionally on public routes (empty identity → check_forward_auth rejects → anonymous). Management routes keep the standard required forward_auth (redirect on 401). Bonus: SSO gives real logout via /oauth2/sign_out.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: UPDATE (.14 landed the display cookie): SSO no longer needs the optional auth-subrequest on public routes for chrome. indice sets its own signed display cookie at /manage/login regardless of proxy, and reads it on public pages. So the SSO Caddyfile only needs the STANDARD required forward_auth on /manage + write /api (redirect-to-login on 401) — no handle_response/graceful-401 gymnastics. SSO's remaining wins over the basic_auth stopgap: real login/logout (/oauth2/sign_out should also clear indice_session), and identity from the IdP instead of a shared password.

comments.text: PR #105 (off main). compose.sso.yaml + Caddyfile.sso: oauth2-proxy GitHub provider (allow-list single user), Caddy forward_auth subrequest on /manage+write-/api with 302→/oauth2/start on 401, identity → X-Forwarded-User + injected secret; public routes straight to indice (display cookie handles chrome). Real logout via INDICE_LOGOUT_REDIRECT=/oauth2/sign_out?rd=/. Scope reduced to user:email (no read:org). README signposts Basic-vs-SSO ladder. VERIFIED end-to-end with a real GitHub login (edsu). Ready to merge.

title: Forward-auth: management chrome missing on public pages + no login affordance
description:
In forward-auth deployments (Caddy basic_auth / future SSO), a signed-in admin sees the workroom chrome + edit-in-place controls ONLY on gated routes (/manage/*, /api/*), NOT on public pages (homepage, collection, crawl). Local --manage mode shows the chrome everywhere, so the two modes are inconsistent. Also there's no way to discover you CAN log in (no login button).

ROOT CAUSE: server.rs admin_ctx() grants chrome only when check_forward_auth() sees the identity header + X-Indice-Auth-Secret. Caddyfile.manage injects those only on the @manage matcher (/manage/* + /api/* except /api/search), so public-route requests never carry them → admin_ctx returns (false, None) on public pages even for a logged-in admin.

FIX (two parts):
1. Caddy opportunistic identity forwarding on public routes. The browser sends 'Authorization: Basic' on every same-origin request once logged in, so add a public handle block matched by @authed (header Authorization *) that runs basic_auth and injects X-Forwarded-User + the secret WHEN present, while the fall-through handle stays anonymous. Use a Caddy snippet (e.g. (indice_authed)) imported by both the @manage and @authed handles to avoid duplication. Anonymous visitors (no Authorization header) are unaffected → clean public site; logged-in admins get (true, Some(user)) on every page → chrome everywhere, matching local mode.
2. indice login affordance in the header (views.rs). When state.forward_auth.is_some(): show 'Log in' if not signed in, 'Signed in as {user}' if signed in. Add a tiny gated GET /manage/login?next=... handler in server.rs that triggers the browser auth prompt and 302s back to next (default /).

CAVEATS: (a) opportunistic block 401s an admin with STALE/changed creds on public pages until they re-auth — only affects people who've logged in, never anonymous visitors; (b) real logout is unreliable with HTTP Basic (browser caches creds) — defer clean login/logout to the oauth2-proxy/SSO work (deploy-wo6l.13). (c) pages now vary by Authorization → ensure public HTML isn't shared-cached as admin-chromed (indice doesn't aggressively cache HTML today; verify).

Relates to admin epic rustyweb-admin-mode-r67p and the SSO upgrade deploy-wo6l.13. Touches Caddyfile.manage, crates/indice-lib/src/views.rs (header), crates/indice-lib/src/server.rs (/manage/login).
close_reason: Merged via PR #104: forward-auth workroom chrome on public pages via a signed display-only cookie, /manage/login + /logout, no-store HTML. Verified in-browser + curl; code-review addressed.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: PR #104 (off main). Fixed via a signed display-only cookie (indice sets indice_session on gated requests; admin_ctx reads header OR cookie → chrome on public pages). Root cause confirmed in-browser: Basic-auth creds aren't sent to parent path / (hard-reload still anonymous, not caching). Added Log in (/manage/login, Referer bounce) + Log out (/logout clears cookie), no-store on HTML (bfcache), session cookie (dies with browser, matches Basic creds), .env gitignored. Code-review (high) run: fixed no-store/backslash-open-redirect/session-cookie/dedup; finding on 12h-public-browsing accepted as minor. Verified in real browser + cookie-jar curl. Logout is display-only (Basic keeps creds until browser close); real sign-out tracked with SSO .13.

title: Push the Homebrew formula automatically on release
description: Once there are 2+ release channels (Homebrew tap deploy-wo6l.8 + Scoop bucket deploy-wo6l.9, and possibly crates.io later), automate the post-release manifest bumps instead of the per-channel manual step documented in RELEASING.md. Add a first-party job to .github/workflows/release.yml (gated to final releases, like the :latest image logic) that, after the binaries publish: regenerates the Homebrew formula (scripts/homebrew-formula.sh) and pushes it to edsu/homebrew-indice, and regenerates the Scoop manifest and pushes it to the scoop bucket. Needs a token with contents:write on the channel repos (a fine-grained PAT, e.g. secret PACKAGE_CHANNELS_TOKEN or per-repo tokens) since the workflow's built-in GITHUB_TOKEN only writes to edsu/indice. Keep it first-party (git + gh + our generator scripts; no third-party bump actions, per supply-chain preference). User is fine with the documented manual step until Scoop lands; revisit then.
notes:
RESCOPED 2026-09-10: Homebrew only. Scoop (deploy-wo6l.9) is closed as not
needed at this stage, so drop the "Scoop manifest" half and the "wait until
there are 2+ channels" framing this bead was originally built on.

That framing was the reason this sat unaddressed, and it had it backwards: with
exactly ONE channel plus a manual step, the case for automating is stronger, not
weaker. The tap is the only part of releasing that lives outside the release
workflow, so it's the only part with no gate — forget it and `brew upgrade
indice` silently keeps installing the previous version, with nothing red
anywhere.

Scope now: a job in .github/workflows/release.yml, gated to final (non-
prerelease) tags exactly like the existing :latest image logic, that regenerates
the formula with scripts/homebrew-formula.sh, VERIFIES its sha256 values against
the release's published .sha256 assets, then commits and pushes to
edsu/homebrew-indice. First-party only (git + gh + our generator).

STATUS: parked at Ed's request 2026-09-10 — no bandwidth for the token right
now. Blocked on a fine-grained PAT with contents:write on edsu/homebrew-indice,
stored as a repo secret (e.g. PACKAGE_CHANNELS_TOKEN); the workflow's built-in
GITHUB_TOKEN can only write to edsu/indice. Nothing to do until that exists.

One design decision to settle when picking this up: if the secret is missing,
the job should FAIL loudly rather than skip silently — a silent skip recreates
the exact "forgot the formula, nothing went red" failure this is meant to fix.

title: docker-compose + Caddyfile (auto-HTTPS) with verified range passthrough
description: docker compose up brings up indice (bound to the compose network, non-root, read-only serve) behind Caddy with automatic HTTPS — the one-command self-host recipe. Caddyfile must pass HTTP Range/Accept-Ranges/Content-Range through to /files/{id} untouched and not buffer multi-GB WACZs, and must NOT gzip range responses (indice already compresses in-process). comments.author: edsu
comments.text: Management-in-container note (2026-08-29): --manage local-trust mode CANNOT run in a container — it refuses non-loopback binds, and a container must bind 0.0.0.0 to be reachable (the guard fires even when the host only publishes to 127.0.0.1, since indice only sees its own 0.0.0.0 bind). So containerized management = forward-auth only. The compose recipe should offer two shapes: (1) plain read-only 'serve' behind Caddy (auto-HTTPS); (2) a management variant: 'serve --manage --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 --auth-proxy-header X-Forwarded-Email' with an SSO layer (e.g. oauth2-proxy) in front and INDICE_AUTH_PROXY_SECRET set + Caddy injecting X-Indice-Auth-Secret. Management writes to /data, so a persistent volume writable by the nonroot uid (65532) is required. Byte-range passthrough still applies to both.

title: Sign + notarize macOS (and Windows) release binaries
description: Prebuilt release binaries are unsigned, so macOS Gatekeeper quarantines the download (first run blocked until 'xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./indice') and Windows SmartScreen warns on the unsigned .exe. Sign + notarize to remove that friction. macOS: Apple Developer Program membership ($99/yr), a Developer ID Application cert, CI secrets (cert .p12 + App Store Connect API key / app-specific password), then codesign -> xcrun notarytool submit --wait -> stapler staple in the release workflow; drop the xattr note from the README. Windows: an Authenticode code-signing cert (paid) + signtool. Deferred from deploy-wo6l.1 (unsigned binaries + documented workaround shipped first). Keep the workflow first-party where possible.

comments.author: edsu
comments.text: Design notes from discussion (2026-08-29): (1) Moving OFF upload-rust-binary-action to the DIY first-party workflow makes signing EASIER, not harder — it exposes the seams to insert codesign (mac) / signtool (windows) between build and packaging, all with native tools, no third-party action. (2) You can't staple a notarization ticket to a BARE CLI binary — stapling only works on .app/.dmg/.pkg. For indice (a CLI) the natural macOS shape is a .pkg that installs indice into /usr/local/bin, which you sign (productsign), notarize, and staple; alternatively notarize the .zip and rely on Gatekeeper's online ticket check. (3) Do packaging + signing together (the signing flow shapes the .pkg build), rather than building unsigned installers first.

title: Ship as a double-click desktop app for individual (non-CLI) users
description:
Make the tool installable and usable by non-technical individuals with no command line.

CONTEXT
- Today: install = cargo install --git (needs Rust 1.97 toolchain); run = CLI index then serve then open browser manually. Hard wall for non-technical users.
- The UI is already a web app (server-rendered maud in views.rs + client-side ReplayWeb.page). Replay REQUIRES a real browser engine: service worker + IndexedDB + HTTP range over http://. No native GUI today.
- serve opens the index READ-ONLY on purpose (server.rs:63) so it never blocks a concurrent CLI index. So add-archive-from-UI is an OPT-IN management mode, not the default.
- Decision (edsu): target macOS + Windows; full desktop WINDOW via embedded webview (Tauri); add archives in the UI; KEEP CLI index/serve unchanged for institutional/service deployments.

ARCHITECTURE
- New crate crates/indice-app (Tauri v2) depends on indice-lib. Binds axum to 127.0.0.1:0, runs it in-process, opens a window at http://127.0.0.1:<port> (real http origin, NOT tauri:// — so service workers work).
- Management mode is opt-in (serve --manage, default off). CLI stays read-only + unchanged.

TWO FLAGGED RISKS/COSTS
1. macOS WKWebView service-worker support is historically finicky (Windows WebView2 is Chromium, fine). VALIDATED GO by the Phase 0 spike (.1, 2026-07-30): replay works in embedded WKWebView given (a) an Info.plist NSAllowsLocalNetworking ATS exception for http://127.0.0.1 and (b) a real .app bundle identity for a persistent SW data store. No system-browser fallback needed on macOS. Windows/WebView2 still to confirm before packaging.
2. Code signing is the tax on double-click: Apple Developer ID (~$99/yr, notarization) + Windows Authenticode, or Gatekeeper/SmartScreen block it.

RENAME (DONE)
- The rustyweb->indice rename is complete; the product name is LOCKED to "indice". Packaging/branding (.6) is no longer gated on it: the macOS bundle id, signing identity, .dmg/.msi names, release URLs, and app data dir all use "indice".
close_reason:
ABANDONED 2026-09-27, Ed's call: the Tauri work is far out of date. The code and its branch were deleted.

HISTORY WORTH KEEPING, because the reasoning was sound at each step and a future desktop attempt should not relitigate it:

The epic was P1 until 2026-08-03, when Ed paused it on the grounds that a desktop app is a *packaging* concern wrapping an experience with no front door: you still could not create a collection or add a crawl except from the CLI. That diagnosis held up. The browser-first admin track that replaced it (rustyweb-admin-mode-r67p) shipped the write surface, and the workroom now does collections, uploads, add-by-path/URL with live progress, finding aids and imports. The thing the desktop app was meant to make approachable got solved without it.

The pieces, and where they went:
- .1 spike DONE=GO. ReplayWeb.page does fully replay in an embedded WKWebView (wry, the engine Tauri v2 uses) against an in-process server, given ATS local-networking, .app bundle identity and an http origin. Those findings are about macOS rather than our code, so they stay true.
- .2 app shell was built and never merged (PR #72); code now deleted.
- .3 add-crawl endpoints were re-homed to the admin epic and shipped.
- .4 empty first-run state re-homed.
- .5/.6 closed with the shell.
- .7 prebuilt CLI binaries: DELIVERED, by the deploy epic. Never Tauri-specific.

What survives in main: indice_lib::server::serve_on_listener (server/mod.rs, covered by tests/app_server.rs), which is the hook that let the app run axum in-process. So embedding is still possible; the shell is what would have to be rewritten.

Reopen only if someone wants a native wrapper *and* is prepared to rebuild the shell against current Tauri.

title: Spike: prove ReplayWeb.page works in an embedded webview (go/no-go)
description:
Throwaway spike. Minimal Tauri window -> existing serve on a localhost port -> confirm a real page REPLAYS: service worker registers, range reads hit /files/{id}, IndexedDB populates. Test on BOTH macOS (WKWebView) and Windows (WebView2). Point the webview at http://127.0.0.1:<port> (NOT tauri://).
GO: proceed with full-window plan. NO-GO (macOS fails): fall back to launch-server + open SYSTEM browser (still a double-click app, no embedded window). Record the decision before Phase 1.
close_reason: done

comments.author: edsu
comments.text:
SPIKE RESULT: GO. Proved ReplayWeb.page replays inside an embedded WKWebView. Method: built a throwaway wry 0.56 + tao 0.36 app (wry is the exact webview engine Tauri v2 renders through, so GO here => GO for the Tauri app shell .2), wrapped in a minimal .app bundle, pointed at 'indice serve' on http://127.0.0.1 with a 4.5MB WACZ (arcgis) indexed into a scratch home. A real archived page RENDERED/replayed in the window (visually confirmed by edsu) — which requires SW registration + ranged /files/ byte reads + IndexedDB, so all three work.

FINDINGS for .2/.3:
1. macOS WKWebView blocks cleartext http:// by default (ATS). The embedded webview MUST ship an Info.plist NSAppTransportSecurity/NSAllowsLocalNetworking=true exception to load http://127.0.0.1. Tauri sets this up but verify it stays enabled.
2. Service workers require a stable app IDENTITY: run from a proper .app bundle with a CFBundleIdentifier so WKWebView gets a persistent website data store. A bare cargo binary is not a faithful test. Persistence confirmed to survive relaunch.
3. Point the webview at the real http://127.0.0.1:<port> origin (NOT a custom/tauri:// scheme) — required for SW.

Windows/WebView2 (Chromium) still UNTESTED here — lower risk, but the go/no-go for Windows should be confirmed on a Windows box before packaging (.6).

Throwaway spike lived in the session scratchpad (not committed).

title: App shell: indice-app Tauri crate that launches + opens a window
description:
New crate crates/indice-app (Tauri v2) depending on indice-lib. Bind axum to 127.0.0.1:0 (free port), spawn server on a tokio task in-process, read the actual port, open a Tauri window at http://127.0.0.1:<port>. Quit-on-window-close ends the process/server task. Default --home to a platform data dir via the directories crate (~/Library/Application Support/indice on macOS, %APPDATA%\indice on Windows); CLI default --home . unchanged.
Add crates/indice-app to the workspace Cargo.toml. Result: double-click -> window opens -> search/browse/replay a populated home.

SPIKE (.1, DONE 2026-07-30 = GO) constraints confirmed on macOS WKWebView, must hold in the real app:
- Info.plist NSAppTransportSecurity / NSAllowsLocalNetworking = true, or WKWebView silently refuses to load the cleartext http://127.0.0.1 origin.
- Run from a real .app bundle with a CFBundleIdentifier so service workers get a persistent website data store (a bare binary is not sufficient / not a faithful test).
- Point the webview at the real http://127.0.0.1 origin, NOT a tauri:// custom scheme (SW requires it).
Tauri normally handles the ATS/bundle-id setup, but verify these survive in the generated config. Windows/WebView2 (Chromium) not yet spiked.

Endpoints: POST /api/archives (takes a local filesystem path from the native dialog; optional byte-upload for browser fallback) -> job id; SSE progress endpoint backed by a NEW index::IndexProgress impl that forwards to a channel (mirror BarProgress at main.rs:480). REUSE index::index_path / index::index_location (the same calls the CLI uses at main.rs:688). After indexing, reload the read-only searcher so new results appear. CLI index remains for service users.

title: Build a WACZ from WARC files (with metadata) and index it
description:
Add `indice wacz build <warcs>... --collection <NAME>`: package one or more WARC files (+ metadata) into a WACZ under <home>/archive and index it via the normal pipeline. The reusable, headless library builder (build_wacz) is also the building block for the Archive-It importer (kx53).

FINALIZED APPROACH (planned 2026-08-20; mirror Webrecorder's own implementation so output replays in ReplayWeb.page/wabac.js):
- Native Rust in a new crates/indice-lib/src/wacz_build.rs (no py-wacz/js-wacz/Node/Python runtime dep; single-binary preserved). Reuse existing zip + warc.rs + wacz.rs.
- WARCs COPIED VERBATIM (byte-for-byte) into archive/<basename>.warc.gz as zip CompressionMethod::Stored — preserve original crawl bytes + digests; never re-serialize (matches browsertrix-crawler util/wacz.ts, which uses client-zip = STORE-only). CDX offsets are READ from the original file via warc.rs iter_records/collect_records_gz.
- Sniff-test each input WARC first (same pass that reads CDX offsets): valid WARC/1.x, per-record members gunzip, >=1 indexable record; else bail with a clear error and produce no WACZ.
- CDX mirrors warcio.js CDXIndexer: CDXJ line '<urlkey> <14-digit-ts> {url,mime,status,digest,length,offset,filename}'; urlkey=getSurt (ported verbatim from warcio.js src/lib/utils.ts via the url crate: strip www\d*., lowercase whole URL, reverse host labels, port if present, pathname, sort query params); digest = WARC payload digest with sha256: prefix stripped (base32, copied not recomputed); exclude request+warcinfo; sort C-locale; plain indexes/index.cdxj (ZipNum >=50KB is a follow-up).
- datapackage.json in browsertrix shape (resources[]{name,path,bytes,hash:sha256:<hex>}, created, wacz_version 1.1.1, software, title?, description?, relation?) plus additive descriptive fields indice reads for finding-aid seeding (mainPageUrl/keywords/licenses/organization). datapackage-digest.json {path,hash}. pages/pages.jsonl (header + seed pages).
- CLI: new Wacz{action} group; metadata from flags mirroring 'collection set'; interactive TTY prompts when stdin().is_terminal() (reuse confirm()), require flags + exit(2) in CI; then index_path().
- VERIFICATION: (a) build->index->search round-trip on fixtures (simple/post/a.warc.gz), cross-check page_count vs reference a.wacz; (b) verbatim-integrity (packaged WARC byte-identical to input); (c) sniff-test negatives; (d) reference-oracle: dev/CI-only Node script runs warcio.js CDXIndexer over fixtures and diffs full CDXJ line-for-line vs ours (gated so plain cargo test needs no Node). Byte-identical WACZ is an explicit NON-GOAL (nondeterministic mtimes/created/gzip); line-for-line CDX conformance is the meaningful guarantee.

Plan file: ~/.claude/plans/wild-dreaming-thacker.md. Follow-ups split to their own beads: ZipNum CDX, browser replay test, HTML title extraction, WACZ signing, --recompress opt-in.
